newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombia banana boss sees '97 exports up 12.6 pct.
newsitem.headline: Colombia banana boss sees '97 exports up 12.6 pct.

text.p: Colombia's banana exports are on target to rise about 12.6 percent this year compared with 1996, the head of one of the country's biggest banana trading companies said Thursday.
Alberto Leon Mejia, chairman of Uniban, said exports should rise to about 80 million 18-kg boxes by the end of the year from 71 million boxes last year.
In the first five months of the year, banana exports were up 14.7 percent to a total value of $206.7 million compared to $180.1 million in the same period in 1996, Mejia said.
Banana export prices averaged $6.06 per box through the first five months of the year, up from an average of $5.75 in the January-May period last year.

Mejia said Colombia's banana industry was one of the most indebted within the country's agricultural sector. But he said improving export prices and a decline in political violence in northwest Uraba, the main banana-growing region, had put the industry on the road to recovery.

Uraba has been the scene of some of Colombia's most violent conflicts over the last 10 years as right-wing paramilitaries and leftist guerrilla groups vied for political and economic control of the area.
Colombia is the world's third largest banana producer after Ecuador and Costa Rica.
